record_title: Quantitative deficiency exponents for distinct consecutive products
provenance: A quantitative refinement of the prime-gap construction in arXiv:2609.17543v1. The split-product integral-point sum is sharpened by isolating the sparse degree-two locus r=2s, and the resulting transfer estimate is combined with the 1/24 almost-all short-prime theorem.
limitations: Originality is to the best of our knowledge. The power-saving 19/24+epsilon bound applies to the total length of short rejected gaps; the full deficiency is bounded by arbitrary negative powers of log X because long gaps are controlled through an exceptional-set theorem. No matching lower bound or optimality statement is claimed. The conclusion inherits the structural construction and witness-forest lemmas of arXiv:2609.17543v1. A closely related September 2026 Zenodo preprint by Ryan Kielhorn (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21287064) was identified as the main residual originality risk: indexed metadata were inspected, but its full preprint text was not. No independent validation or formal proof-assistant verification is asserted for this record.

artifact_inventory.description: Exact rational verification of limiting exponents, monotonicity coefficients, and the degree-two locus identity.
